questions: If N != M, is the maximum number of pairs we can choose limited by min(N, M), or can we choose fewer pairs than that?
Are we allowed to choose zero balls (i.e., zero black and zero white)?
Should we maximize the sum of values, or simply compute the sum for a given choice? The phrase 'Among all such choices, find the sum of the values of the chosen balls' is ambiguous.
Can we choose the same ball multiple times?
If there are multiple ways to achieve the same maximum sum, does it matter which one we output?
Are the balls distinguishable only by value, or do indices matter for uniqueness?
Should the sum be printed as an integer without any formatting (like newline)?
If all values are negative, is the optimal sum simply the least negative sum (i.e., still maximizing), or could zero be better if allowed?
